system_description.narrative_title: Iran's Economic Survival and Geopolitical Pivot under U.S. Pressure
system_description.narrative_summary: Across the window, the dominant narrative is that escalating U.S. pressure and the risk of wider conflict are driving Iran to pivot economically and strategically — developing a 'survival economy', deepening ties with BRICS and alternative payment systems, and tightening internal political control. That pivot is producing measurable global spillovers (higher mortgage costs, shifts in regional defense demand, trade and technology winners) and creating feedbacks that complicate both Washington's coercive options and Tehran's resilience. The system is open: external sanctions, diplomatic signals, commodity and financial markets, and regional security dynamics all interact and adapt.
system_description.scope: Actors, states, and processes directly shaping or responding to U.S.–Iran confrontation and Iran's economic pivot: Iranian political leadership and economy, U.S. policy choices (economic pressure and military options), BRICS financial institutions and payment/CBDC initiatives, regional defense and trade demand (Middle East partners), global financial and commodity market responses, and domestic Iranian economic behaviors (consumption, credit, 'survival economy' adaptations).
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic order (international security + international finance/trade regimes).
adjacent_subsystems: International financial architecture and sanctions regime (payments, CBDCs, reserve alternatives)
Regional Middle East security and defense procurement
Global trade/supply chains and export sectors (e.g., China’s manufacturing/export winners)

variables.name: Sanctions and economic pressure intensity
variables.description: The overall severity and frequency of external economic coercion measures applied to the target economy (trade restrictions, asset freezes, financial exclusion).

variables.name: Military escalation risk
variables.description: The perceived probability and momentum of kinetic conflict widening or intensifying in the regional security environment.

variables.name: Survival economy adaptation
variables.description: The rate and depth at which informal exchanges, barter, rationing, and low-capital economic practices expand within the domestic economy.

variables.name: Alternative payment system integration
variables.description: The extent of integration with non-mainstream cross-border payment channels and alternative settlement arrangements.

variables.name: Internal political control strength
variables.description: The degree of centralized authority, coercive capacity, and institutional consolidation within the domestic political system.

variables.name: Trade diversion rate
variables.description: The flux of export and import volumes being reoriented away from traditional partners toward alternative trading relationships.

variables.name: Currency and capital stability
variables.description: The stability of the exchange rate and the net pace of capital flows, including capital flight and capital controls effectiveness.

variables.name: Inflation and cost-of-living pressure
variables.description: The trend level of consumer price increases and resulting real-income erosion experienced by households.

variables.name: Household credit and payment-pattern shift
variables.description: The rate at which consumers move toward deferred-payment, credit-based, or informal financing mechanisms for consumption.

variables.name: Regional defense procurement demand
variables.description: The aggregate demand growth for military and defense-related goods and services across neighboring states and markets.

variables.name: Global commodity price volatility
variables.description: The variance and sensitivity of major commodity prices (energy, metals, food) to shocks originating from the regional confrontation.

variables.name: Cross-border financial cooperation level
variables.description: The stock of formalized financial linkages and cooperative arrangements among alternative banking and development networks.

variables.name: Sanctions evasion capacity
variables.description: The capability and resources available to bypass external financial and trade restrictions (networks, intermediaries, workaround mechanisms).

variables.name: Regime legitimacy perception
variables.description: Popular and elite perceptions of the governing authority's legitimacy and its social mandate to govern.

variables.name: Shift toward alternative geopolitical alignments
variables.description: The rate at which the polity reorients diplomatic and strategic partnerships away from established networks toward alternative blocs or partners.

variables.name: External diplomatic pressure signals
variables.description: The intensity and clarity of non-economic diplomatic communications and demands from external actors directed at the polity.

catalysts.title: Iran joins BRICS development bank
catalysts.description: Formal accession to the BRICS development bank (membership/operational link) that increases Iran's access to non-Western financing and projects.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran to join BRICS development bank soon' (Reuters, FT).

catalysts.title: BRICS payment/CBDC linking talks advance
catalysts.description: Ongoing BRICS discussions on linking payment systems and CBDCs that enable alternative settlement channels for members, including Iran.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'BRICS nations discuss linking payment systems and CBDCs' (RBI chief).

catalysts.title: Pakistan-facilitated U.S.–Iran deal progress
catalysts.description: Negotiation momentum (reparations/conditions) mediated by Pakistan that could reduce diplomatic tensions and economic coercion if a deal advances.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Pakistan signals progress on U.S.-Iran deal as Washington and Tehran trade reparation demands.'

catalysts.title: Renewed U.S. economic pressure campaign
catalysts.description: A sustained U.S. strategy to intensify sanctions and economic coercion aimed at forcing Iranian concessions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump Shifts to Economic Pressure, Again' and 'Trump says ... let Tehran fail economically or 'hit them really hard''.

catalysts.title: Expansion of survival economy and 'buy now, pay later'
catalysts.description: Rapid growth of informal survival practices and consumer shifts to deferment/alternative credit as living costs rise.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran Is Defying U.S. Pressure by Becoming a ‘Survival Economy’' and 'Iranians opt to ‘buy now, pay later’'.

catalysts.title: Supreme leader elevates loyalists — consolidation
catalysts.description: Political consolidation via promotions and appointments, tightening centralized control and security oversight.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran’s supreme leader elevates loyalists as he tightens grip' — indicates consolidation.

catalysts.title: Regional defense procurement surge
catalysts.description: Higher regional demand for defense equipment as states hedge amid the Iran war, boosting arms procurement cycles.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'TKMS sees increased demand from Middle East following Iran war' and related war coverage.

catalysts.title: Rising mortgage costs and credit squeeze
catalysts.description: Higher borrowing costs and mortgage spreads that reduce household balance-sheet capacity and push alternative financing.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'FirstFT: Iran war pushes up mortgage costs' and 'Mortgage costs pushed higher by US stand-off with Iran.'

catalysts.title: China export surge to region (e-trucks)
catalysts.description: Increased Chinese commercial exports to the region that redirect trade flows and bolster non-Western supply links.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran war a boon for China's e-trucks, fuelling export surge.'
